question: Which government will form after the 2026 New Zealand general election?

calls.reasoning: Polls show National and Labour tied (~28%); right bloc Nat+ACT+NZF ~48-50% vs left Lab+Grn+TPM ~44-45%, with Opportunity (5-8%) as kingmaker. Luxon ruled out TOP, but TOP says it will approach the largest party first and has floated dropping tax reform; its bottom lines lean left. If TOP misses 5%, the right bloc is favoured through wasted vote. Polymarket next-PM (Luxon ~56%, Hipkins ~45%, not deadline-matched) and party-in-government markets (Nat 0.56, Lab 0.49, thin) agree with a slight National edge. Timing: election 7 Nov, official results 27 Nov; the 2023-style ~40-day path lands around 17 Dec, so missing the January deadline is a real tail, especially for a 4-party Labour deal.
calls.dossier:
- Election Sat 7 Nov 2026; official results incl. special votes declared 27 Nov 2026 (Electoral Commission key dates; RNZ explainer).
- 1News-Verian 8-12 Oct: Nat 28, Lab 28, Grn 15, ACT 10, NZF 10, TPM 0.4, TOP 8; seats Nat 34, Lab 34, Grn 18, ACT 12, NZF 12, TPM 4, TOP 10. Neither bloc has a majority without TOP (Wikipedia polling page; 1News 13 Oct).
- Other Oct polls: Anacta 6-10 Oct Nat 28 Lab 29 TOP 5.4; TPU-Curia 1-5 Oct Nat 28.5 Lab 28.2 NZF 12 TOP 4.8; Reid Research 24 Sep-1 Oct Nat 25.9 Lab 30.8 TOP 5.5; Roy Morgan Aug-Sep Nat 31 Lab 23.5 TOP 6.5. One mid-Oct news report says a poll had the incumbent coalition on 61/120 seats with TOP at 6.1%.
- TOP polls between 4.8 and 8%; if it falls below 5% with no electorate seat, its votes are wasted, which tends to help the larger bloc.
- Luxon has repeatedly ruled out working with TOP over its land tax (NZ Herald 8 Oct). TOP leader Qiulae Wong says TOP will approach the largest party first and might pause tax reform for significant policy wins. Hipkins says Labour's door is open to TOP.
- TOP's bottom lines lean left (Newsroom 30 Sep). TOP voters lean Labour, but the party says that does not drive its decision (RNZ).
- ACT's Seymour hinted at a possible arrangement with TOP, a 'four-headed beast' (RNZ headline, Oct).
- Campaign: Greens/TPM gang hui photo controversy (mid-Oct). National ruled out tax cuts in its fiscal plan. Possible TPM overhang complicates the seat maths.
- Formation timing history: 2023 election 14 Oct, finals ~3 Nov, deal 24 Nov (~40 days from election day). 2017 election 23 Sep, Peters decision 19 Oct, sworn in 26 Oct. 40 days from 7 Nov is about 17 Dec.
- Status quo: the National-ACT-NZF government continues; a caretaker government does not count.
- Resolution instrument: resolves off the government appointed by the Governor-General (NZ Government / 55th Parliament seating plan), not off election-night results or markets.
- Event window: election 7 Nov 2026 -> government must be formed before 1 Jan 2027 per the criteria; as of 18 Oct 2026 the election has not yet happened (0% of the post-election window elapsed).
- Searched but not found: an exact-match market on 'government formed before January'; a firm Luxon reversal on TOP.
calls.reference_class: NZ MMP elections 1996-2023: share forming a government within ~6 weeks of election day, and incumbent-led bloc outcomes in near-tied polls

calls.reasoning: Polls put National and Labour level at about 28%. Blocs are near 58-65 (right) vs 53-57+TOP (left), and TOP holds the balance in most recent polls. National has ruled out TOP, so whenever TOP is kingmaker Labour-led is favoured. The right wins outright if it reaches 61 (Curia-style polls, TOP falling below 5%, a polling miss). The incumbent continuing is a slight edge for the status quo. Government formation must finish within about 5 weeks of the 27 Nov special-vote release (2023 took 6 weeks from election day), so there is a non-trivial chance nothing is formed before January. Polymarket per-party markets are thin ($3k total) and roughly equal for National and Labour; I found no exact-match market on Manifold or with bookmakers, and Kalshi was not checked.

calls.reasoning: Polls are tied near 28% each; Opportunity (5-8%) is the projected kingmaker. Projections differ: latest 1News-Verian has Labour+Greens+TOP+TPM at 66/124, while Taxpayers' Union-Curia has the incumbent National+ACT+NZF at 65/120. National has ruled out any TOP deal including confidence and supply. Labour courts TOP, and TOP's bottom lines lean left, so a hung result favours Labour unless National reverses. Polymarket's thin participation markets (National 0.56, Labour 0.49 'part of govt') imply a near coin-flip. The timing risk is real: official results come 27 Nov, and the 2023 lag of 24 days to swearing-in would mean about 21 Dec. A complex four-party left deal could slip past 1 Jan. Other-led is negligible.

calls.reasoning: National and Labour are tied near 28%. The right bloc (Nat+ACT+NZF, ~48-50%) leads the left (Lab+Grn+TPM, ~44-45%), and TOP (4.8-8%) is the likely kingmaker. National has ruled TOP out, so Labour is favoured when TOP holds the balance. The right wins outright if TOP misses 5% or Curia-type polls are right, and National could also reverse on TOP, which gives National a slight edge. Election 7 Nov, official results 27 Nov, 55 days to the deadline; past formations (2017 ~33 days, 2023 ~44 days) mostly fit, so the deadline-miss tail is modest. Thin Polymarket participation markets (Nat 0.56, Lab 0.49) are near-miss evidence only.
calls.reconciliation: The runs differed only slightly. Factual: the seat projections conflict (Verian: left+TOP 66/124; Curia: right 65/120) because the polls disagree on TOP's vote share around the 5% threshold. This is real uncertainty and cannot be settled without new data. The timing facts are consistent across dossiers (results 27 Nov; 2023 took ~44 days, 2017 ~33, 1996 ~65 against a 55-day window), so I put the deadline miss at 7%, slightly below the runs' 9-10%, because of Christmas pressure and quick formation after a clear result. Judgment: I give National a slight edge on its bloc vote-share lead, TOP's wasted-vote risk, and the chance National backs down on TOP. I retrieved nothing new this run.
